newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields ended the week lower on Friday as a stronger crown helped dealers to shrug off Thursday's rise in U.S. debt yields.
The Swedish market also found some support in stronger Italian and Spanish markets.
But U.S. economic figures, published after Friday's closing of the Stockholm market, painted a gloomy picture for Monday's trade.
"We saw nine-year bond yields jump four basis points after the market closed, and that will set the tone for Monday," said one dealer.
The crown firmed versus the mark, mainly following moves in the dollar/mark cross. At 1430 GMT, the mark had eased to 4.4735/85 crowns from 4.4760 crowns on Thursday afternoon.
Dealers were focusing on speculations of an announcement of a Finnish ERM (Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism) link this weekend but were divided on the prospect of Sweden following.

Some expected the crown to firm if Finland decided to link the markka to ERM. Others forecast crown selling for markkas as Sweden's ruling Social Democrat party was seen taking a wait-and-see stance on Swedish participation.
